description:
Castello di Vicarello is a historic residence dating back to the year 1100. In 1979, Carlo and Aurora Baccheschi Berti bought the then-abandoned castle to make it their family home, beginning a restoration process that lasted 18 years. The result was a careful recovery of the 12th-century structure, set within 40 hectares of century-old vineyards and olive groves at the heart of the Tuscan Maremma.

In 2003 the family opened the castle as a hotel, keeping its character as an intimate family project — just 10 suites in total — and in 2024 it reopened with new suites following an additional renovation. The complex today combines the main castle building, with its tower and views toward the Tyrrhenian Sea, with more recent structures spread across the estate, including a former watchtower converted into a villa and a contemporary chalet-style suite.

The Baccheschi Berti family's 18-year restoration, undertaken initially as a private home rather than a commercial venture, gives Vicarello a genuinely personal character distinct from properties restored explicitly for hospitality from the outset.

The estate's mix of antiques and Indonesian-inspired design pieces across its 10 suites reflects a deliberately curated, individually decorated approach rather than a uniform hotel-chain aesthetic — each suite reads as a distinct room rather than one of a standardized set.

The explicit inclusion of a contemporary chalet-style suite alongside the historic castle building and converted watchtower is an unusually direct acknowledgment, within this collection, that not every accommodation on a historic estate needs to imitate a period style.

The surrounding Tuscan Maremma, roughly midway between Rome and Florence, gives guests staying at Vicarello access to the region's coastline, the Brunello wine route around Montalcino, and the natural hot springs at Saturnia.

faqs.question: Are all 10 suites at Castello di Vicarello within the main castle?
faqs.answer: No — only 2 of the 10 suites are in the main castle building (including the Suite Torre, at the top of the main tower). The rest are spread across separate garden buildings, a converted watchtower (Villa La Vedetta), and a contemporary chalet-style building.

faqs.question: Who restored Castello di Vicarello?
faqs.answer: The Baccheschi Berti family, who bought the abandoned castle in 1979 as their private home and restored it over 18 years before opening it as a hotel in 2003.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 1h15 from Grosseto and 1h45 from Rome or Florence by car (the castle sits roughly midway between the two cities); the closest airports are Rome-Fiumicino or Florence-Peretola. A very rural area — a car is essential.

**Rooms & rates:** Just 10 suites: 2 in the main castle building (including the Suite Torre, at the top of the tower), 2 in separate garden buildings, 1 in the converted watchtower (Villa La Vedetta), and 1 in a contemporary chalet-style building. From €550/night.

**On-site:** 2 swimming pools (one among olive trees, one with mountain views), 2 organic kitchen gardens, spa treatments, private sauna and jacuzzi in one suite.

**Good to know:** As a family project with just 10 suites, book well ahead, especially in peak season (spring-autumn).

**Combine with:** The Tuscan Maremma and its coastline, Montalcino and the Brunello wine route (~50 min), and the natural hot springs at Saturnia (~40 min).
